Story 5 worked example, exact. Note fam_oop_met ($6,200) differs from M1006's ($4,500) despite being 'same family, same plan' per the source doc -- this is the spec's own stated numbers, not a data-entry error introduced here. The schema stores fam_ded_met/fam_oop_met per member row rather than in a separate shared-family table specifically to accommodate this: in a real system, per-member cached snapshots of a family aggregate can transiently disagree until reconciled (e.g. one member's row reflects a more recent claim than the other's). Do not silently overwrite one to match the other.
